title: Fuel Metering Unit Delivery Nozzle Change and Cowl Latch Clearance Increase
abstract: Replaces the fuel metering unit delivery nozzle with a variant that holds its spray pattern at low fuel temperature, and increases the clearance at the cowl latch that was found to be contacting the nozzle shroud on the higher rated installation.

sections.reason: Cold soak starts on the higher rated installation showed a longer light-up time and a wider spread between engines, traced to the delivery nozzle spray pattern collapsing at fuel temperatures below minus twenty degrees. Separately, and found during the same investigation, the cowl latch on twelve aircraft showed witness marks against the nozzle shroud, caused by a stack-up between the latch bracket and the shroud that is only present on this installation.
sections.description: The delivery nozzle is replaced by a variant with a revised swirl insert and a two millimetre shorter body, which restores the spray pattern down to minus forty degrees. The nozzle shroud is retained but the cowl latch bracket is replaced by a variant that moves the latch outboard by six millimetres, giving twelve millimetres of clearance to the shroud in the worst stack-up. The mount link and the fuel feed connection are unchanged, so no engine build standard change is required and the units remain shop interchangeable.
sections.effects: Mass reduction of zero point three kilograms per engine. No electrical load change. One way interchangeable: the new nozzle may be fitted to a pre modification engine, but the old nozzle must not be fitted to an aircraft with the relocated latch bracket because the clearance is then unverified. Removal and installation tasks change for the shorter nozzle body and the revised latch torque. Parts catalogue figure reissued with a pre and post item pair.
sections.embodiment_note: Cut in at MSN M00401. Retrofit by bulletin at any engine access opportunity, roughly six hours per engine with the fan cowl open.

type_data.production_impact: Cut in at MSN M00401 with the engine build standard unchanged
